## Goal

Pin the off-peak-windowed, all-opencode low-priority fallback behaviour with tests **before** the config change (test-first).

## Scope

Tests only; no production behaviour change in this item.

## Work

1. **Window gating:** an `available_times`-carrying entry is skipped outside its UTC window (`_is_within_allowed_window` → `Skipping provider=...: outside its available_times window (UTC)`) and selected inside it.
2. **Chain order:** `priority_routes.low` for plan/author/code resolves to `local-qwen3 → munitoai-free → opencode-go-3 → opencode-go-2 → opencode-go`. (Red until the config item lands — intended TDD state; document the convention if the repo requires green main.)
3. **Per-key 429 failover (the key behaviour):** a 429 from `opencode-go-3` must NOT exclude `opencode-go-2` / `opencode-go` from the same request — rate-limit quarantine is keyed on `_usage_limit_account_key` (`api_key_env@endpoint`), so sibling accounts are independent (LP-0MSMBWB23009XYPW, LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N).
4. **Same-domain 5xx caveat:** a 5xx from `opencode-go-3` DOES exclude its same-gateway siblings as one failure domain (`_failure_domain_key` / `attempted_domains`, LP-0MSG45I8Q0020N1F) — assert the honest behaviour so nobody assumes 3× outage resilience.
5. **No paid-tier leak:** `munitoai` and `deepseek-flash` never appear in any `low` chain.
6. **Medium/high unaffected:** those chains are unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Tests cover in-window selection, out-of-window skip-and-fall-through, and behaviour-neutrality when the free tier still has budget.
2. A test asserts the exact 5-entry low chain order for plan, author and code.
3. A test asserts 429-per-account failover lets sibling opencode keys be tried in the same request.
4. A test asserts 5xx does NOT give sibling failover (same failure domain).
5. A test asserts `munitoai` / `deepseek-flash` absent from `low` chains and `medium`/`high` chains unchanged.
6. Reuses existing proxy test conventions (monkeypatched clock for `available_times`, existing timing-gate fixtures) rather than inventing new harness code.
7. full suite green via `/skill:test`, except the documented intentional red chain-order assertion pending the config item.
data.title: Test: off-peak low-priority fallback gating

# Quota poller and derived state (tracer bullet)

## Goal

Give the proxy a proactive, authoritative per-account view of each
`opencode-*` account's remaining allowance, instead of learning about
exhaustion reactively from a `GoUsageLimitError`.

This is the tracer bullet for LP-0MVF4FIP1001RD8P: it lands the module, the
injectable test transport (the shared harness every later feature is tested
through), the derivation model, the poll-interval config key and the
background poll task — end to end, with tests, in one slice.

## Scope

- New module `proxy/quota_state.py`:
  - `QuotaWindow` / `QuotaSnapshot` dataclasses holding
    `rolling`/`weekly`/`monthly` `percent` + `resetsAt`, plus derived
    `*_headroom`, `seconds_to_reset`, `effective_headroom`, `exhausted`,
    `last_success_at`, `last_status`.
  - Async poller for `GET {endpoint}/v1/usage` with `Authorization: Bearer
    $api_key_env`, `cache-control: no-store` honoured, per-account cache keyed
    on the API-key account (reuse `provider._usage_limit_account_key`
    semantics, not the endpoint).
  - Single-flight coalescing per account (one in-flight task per account) and
    interval gating on `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` (default 900).
  - Injectable module-level transport hook (mirroring
    `provider._usage_limit_probe_transport`) so tests never touch the network.
  - Fail-open on poll error: keep the last known snapshot, log at WARN, never
    raise and never delay a client request.
- Derivation rules: headroom is `100 - percent` per window;
  `effective_headroom` is the **minimum** of the three; a window whose
  `status` is anything other than `"ok"` is treated conservatively as
  exhausted/blocking; a missing or unparseable `resetsAt` yields
  `seconds_to_reset <= 0` (never a guessed value).
- Config: `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` [900] and
  `server.quota_surge_accounts` (optional filter; default = all `opencode-*`
  entries).
- Startup: register the refresh task in `proxy/lifecycle.py` and cancel it on
  shutdown; a failed poll must never break startup.
- Logging: one INFO line per successful poll per account (percent per window +
  seconds to reset); WARN on failure (rate-limited so a dead endpoint does not
  flood the log).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — With a stubbed `/v1/usage` transport, the poller issues at most one
  request per account per `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` (default 900 s)
  no matter how many client requests arrive, and concurrent pollers coalesce
  into a single in-flight request per account.
- AC1b — A poll failure (500, timeout, malformed body) leaves the previous
  values intact, logs at WARN, and never fails or delays a client request.
- AC2a — From a known `/v1/usage` payload the derived state reports, per
  account, `rolling`/`weekly`/`monthly` percent, `resetsAt`,
  `seconds_to_reset` and `effective_headroom`, where `effective_headroom` is
  the **minimum** of the three windows (feed `rolling=95, weekly=10,
  monthly=40` and assert effective headroom is 5).
- AC2b — A window whose `status` is not `"ok"` is treated conservatively as
  blocking (`exhausted`), and a missing/invalid `resetsAt` yields
  `seconds_to_reset <= 0` rather than a guessed value.
- AC1c — Two provider entries sharing one `api_key_env` share one account
  snapshot and one poll (no duplicate upstream `/v1/usage` calls).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `proxy/quota_state.py` with dataclasses, derivation helpers and the
   poller; keep all clocks injectable (`now: Callable[[], datetime]`) so tests
   are deterministic.
2. Expose `get_quota_snapshot(provider_cfg, config)` (cache read, never
   blocking) and `refresh_quota_accounts(model_config, config)` (background
   refresh).
3. Wire the refresh task into `proxy/lifecycle.py` startup/shutdown.
4. Tests in `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py` using the injected transport and
   a frozen clock: interval gating, single-flight, fail-open, derivation
   (including the minimum-of-three case), shared-account de-duplication.

## Key Files

- `proxy/quota_state.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py`
- `proxy/lifecycle.py`
- `proxy/provider.py`

## Dependencies

None — this is the tracer bullet for the epic.

## Deliverables

- `proxy/quota_state.py` (poller + derivation + injectable transport harness)
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_state.py` (unit + harness fixtures reused by later
  features)
- `server.quota_poll_interval_seconds` and `server.quota_surge_accounts`
  config keys (documented later in the docs feature)
- Poll logging (INFO success / WARN failure)

## Test plan

- Fake `/v1/usage` transport returning a fixed payload; frozen clock.
- Interval gating: 10 client calls inside one interval → 1 upstream poll.
- Single-flight: 5 concurrent refreshes → 1 in-flight request.
- Failure paths: 500, timeout, malformed JSON → previous snapshot retained,
  WARN logged, no exception escapes.
- Derivation table including `rolling=95, weekly=10, monthly=40 → 5`, a
  non-`ok` status, and a missing `resetsAt`.
data.title: Quota poller and derived state (tracer bullet)

# Tests: reset-aware account quarantine (test-first, red)

## Goal

As a proxy operator, I want failing tests that pin down the reset-aware,
account-scoped 429 quarantine, so the implementation in the sibling item is
driven by executable expectations rather than prose.

## Parent context

Parent LP-0MVDNP36J006430L ("Respect MunitoAI x-ratelimit-* reset headers on
quota 429s") owns the **account-scoped application** of the reset-derived
cooldown. The generic header-parsing engine already landed in
LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ (completed, commit `1245f383`): `_parse_ratelimit_duration`,
`_parse_ratelimit_reset_seconds`, `_ratelimit_over_limit`,
`_get_respect_ratelimit_headers`, and the provider-entry cooldown applied in
`_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`. LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N (completed) supplied
account-key eligibility: `_is_account_rate_limit_error`,
`_usage_limit_account_key`, and per-request `attempted_domains` poisoning.

**Gap this phase pins down:** a quota 429 carrying a reset header currently
sets only the provider-ENTRY cooldown (`mark_provider_unavailable(name, …)`,
2 s margin, 60 s cap) and never records an account-scoped quarantine in
`_usage_reset_at`. So the reset duration is not persisted, not reflected in
`_compute_retry_after()`, and does not cover a differently-named entry
sharing the same `api_key_env` account.

## Scope

Tests only — no production code changes in this item. New tests must be
**red** (failing) against current `dev` and the red output must be recorded
in a comment before moving on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A test writes a quota 429 body (`type: rate_limit_error`,
      `code: rate_limit_exceeded`) plus `x-ratelimit-reset-requests: 32s`
      (and `x-ratelimit-over-limit: yes`) from a `munitoai-free`-style entry
      with `respect_ratelimit_headers: true`, and asserts the failing
      ACCOUNT key is quarantined in `_usage_reset_at` with
      `_usage_reset_remaining(account) > 0` and an expiry of roughly
      `now + 32 + 120` seconds (parsed reset + the existing
      `_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS` 2-minute margin).
- [ ] AC2 — A test asserts the quarantine is scoped to the failing
      `api_key_env` account key ONLY: the paid sibling
      (`MUNITOAI_API_KEY`-style account) has no `_usage_reset_at` entry, no
      provider cooldown, and `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions` still
      returns it after the 429 (sibling preservation,
      LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N).
- [ ] AC3 — A test asserts a quota 429 carrying a reset header advances the
      chain to the next provider within the same request, and that a quota
      429 exhausting the whole chain still produces the chain-hold
      exhaustion response with a `retry_after` derived from the account
      quarantine (i.e. `_compute_retry_after()` sees `_usage_reset_at`).
- [ ] AC4 — A test asserts unchanged behaviour when no reset signal is
      present: a quota 429 with no `x-ratelimit-*` headers applies the
      existing short provider cooldown, creates NO `_usage_reset_at` entry,
      and poisons only the per-request account key (not the failure domain).
- [ ] AC5 — Regression tests confirm the `FreeUsageLimitError` (3 h
      cooldown) and `GoUsageLimitError` (account quarantine) paths are
      unchanged by the new code path.
- [ ] AC6 — A test asserts the feature-flag gate: with
      `respect_ratelimit_headers` false on the entry (and not enabled
      globally) the reset headers are ignored and no account quarantine is
      created.
- [ ] AC7 — Both fallback loops are covered:
      `_proxy_with_remote_fallback_cycle` and `_proxy_with_fallback_cycle`
      each have at least one reset-aware quarantine assertion, so a fix
      applied to only one loop fails the suite.
- [ ] AC8 — The red test run is recorded in a comment on this work item
      (command + failing test names) before the implementation item starts.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_account_quarantine.py` with the focused
  quarantine/`Retry-After`/flag-gate cases (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7).
- Reuse the existing fixtures and 429 builders in
  `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` (`munitoai_free_paid_chain`,
  `_rate_limit_exceeded_429`) — extend that file for the sibling-eligibility
  case (AC2) rather than duplicating fixtures.
- Use the existing autouse reset fixtures (module-level `_usage_reset_at` /
  `_provider_unavailable_until` clearing) so tests stay order-independent.

## Constraints

- Do NOT re-implement header parsing — call the existing helpers.
- Do NOT weaken or delete the existing account-key poisoning assertions
  (notably `test_account_429_poisons_account_key_not_failure_domain`, whose
  `free_account not in provider._usage_reset_at` assertion must stay valid
  for a reset-header-less 429).
- Tests must not require network access or a live proxy.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_account_quarantine.py` — new focused test module
  for the reset-aware account quarantine.
- `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` — sibling-eligibility and
  per-request exclusion assertions.
- `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_headers_cooldown.py` — existing header-parsing
  and provider-cooldown tests that must keep passing.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only reference for the helpers under test.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first). Blocks the implementation item.

## Deliverables

- New/extended tests, red against current `dev`.
- Red-run evidence recorded as a work-item comment.
data.title: Tests: reset-aware account quarantine (test-first)

# Implement reset-derived account quarantine

## Goal

As a proxy operator, I want a MunitoAI quota 429 that advertises its reset
window to quarantine the failing API-key ACCOUNT for that window, so the free
tier is not re-probed every cycle while paid siblings on the same gateway stay
eligible.

## Scope

Production code only, driven by the red tests from the test-first sibling
item. One change site: the shared HTTP-error primitive
`_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`, which both fallback loops already call.

## Design

- Reuse the merged parsing engine from LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ
  (`_parse_ratelimit_reset_seconds`, `_ratelimit_over_limit`,
  `_get_respect_ratelimit_headers`) — do not parse headers again.
- When the response is a **quota 429** (HTTP 429 AND
  `_is_account_rate_limit_error(response, body_text)` OR
  `_ratelimit_over_limit(response.headers)`) AND the entry opts in via
  `respect_ratelimit_headers` AND a reset duration parses, record an
  account-scoped quarantine:
  `_set_usage_limit_quarantine(_usage_limit_account_key(provider_cfg),
  _UsageLimitReset(reset + _USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS, True, label))`.
  `explicit=True` keeps it persisted to `provider-state.json` and exempt from
  the guessed-quarantine 24 h cap.
- The account key (`api_key_env@endpoint:model`, see
  `_usage_limit_account_key`) is what `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions`
  already consults via `_usage_reset_remaining`, so sibling preservation and
  cross-request skipping come for free with no change to
  `attempted_domains` semantics.
- Keep the existing provider-ENTRY cooldown / exponential backoff and the
  `Retry-After` precedence untouched; the account quarantine is additive and
  is the authoritative record of the upstream reset.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — On a quota 429 with a parseable `x-ratelimit-reset-*` header from
      an opted-in entry, the failing account is quarantined for
      `reset + _USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS` (120 s) and the quarantine
      is persisted (explicit), so it survives a restart.
- [ ] AC2 — The quarantine is ACCOUNT-scoped: no failure-domain or brand
      cooldown is added for a quota 429, and a paid sibling entry on the same
      gateway with a different `api_key_env` remains eligible in the same and
      subsequent requests (LP-0MVCX0E2V001VB5N preserved).
- [ ] AC3 — A missing, zero or unparseable reset (or
      `x-ratelimit-over-limit` without a reset) creates NO account
      quarantine; the pre-existing short provider cooldown plus per-request
      account-key poisoning is applied unchanged.
- [ ] AC4 — `FreeUsageLimitError` (3 h) and `GoUsageLimitError` (explicit
      account quarantine) paths are untouched: their handling runs first and
      the new code path is never reached for them.
- [ ] AC5 — Chain-hold semantics are preserved: a quota-429 account advances
      the chain within the request, and an all-exhausted chain still holds
      (300 s, max 3 cycles, 720 s budget) when the quarantine fits the
      budget, or returns the exhaustion response immediately with the
      quarantine-derived `retry_after` when it does not.
- [ ] AC6 — The attempt record for the reset path carries
      `cooldown_seconds`, `ratelimit_reset_seconds` and `ratelimit_over_limit`
      (existing fields) plus a marker that an account quarantine was applied,
      so the behaviour is observable in diagnostics.
- [ ] AC7 — The changed-scope test gate is green, including all tests created
      by the test-first sibling item.

## Minimal implementation

- Add a small private helper (for example
  `_apply_ratelimit_account_quarantine`) next to the existing
  `_parse_ratelimit_reset_seconds` helpers, which decides whether the
  response is a quota 429 and applies the quarantine, returning the applied
  reset (or `None`) for the attempt record.
- Call it from `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown` where
  `ratelimit_reset` is already computed, immediately before
  `mark_provider_unavailable` — one site covers both fallback loops.
- Keep the provider-entry cooldown line unchanged so the existing
  `Skipping provider=… in cooldown` diagnostics and
  `test_ratelimit_headers_cooldown.py` assertions still hold.

## Constraints

- No new config knobs: reuse `respect_ratelimit_headers`,
  `ratelimit_cooldown_margin_seconds` and the existing 120 s usage-limit
  margin constant.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` only — no changes to routing config, budgets or
  the budget gate.
- Do not change `_compute_retry_after`, `_resolve_provider_with_exclusions`
  or the chain-hold helpers; the new quarantine must be consumed by them
  as-is.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — `_handle_http_error_with_cooldown`, the
  `x-ratelimit-*` helper block, `_set_usage_limit_quarantine`,
  `_usage_limit_account_key`, `_is_account_rate_limit_error`.
- `proxy/tests/test_ratelimit_account_quarantine.py` — the red tests this
  change must turn green.
- `proxy/tests/test_failure_domain_grouping.py` — sibling-eligibility and
  per-request exclusion assertions.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the test-first sibling item (red tests must exist first).

## Deliverables

- Implemented behaviour in `proxy/proxy/provider.py`.
- Green changed-scope test gate; commit recorded on this work item.
data.title: Implement reset-derived account quarantine

# Docs: reset-aware account quarantine

## Goal

As a proxy operator reading the repository docs, I want the reset-aware,
account-scoped 429 quarantine documented next to the existing cooldown and
usage-limit-quarantine descriptions, so the two distinct safety margins and
the sibling-preservation guarantee are discoverable without reading
`provider.py`.

## Scope

Documentation and configuration comments only — no behavioural change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — `proxy/docs/routing.md` ("Upstream rate-limit headers" section)
      documents the account-scoped quarantine: which 429 body/header signals
      trigger it, that the wait is the parsed reset plus the existing
      **2-minute** usage-limit margin (`_USAGE_LIMIT_RESET_MARGIN_SECONDS`),
      how that differs from the **2-second**
      `ratelimit_cooldown_margin_seconds` applied to the provider-entry
      cooldown, and that the account key is
      `api_key_env@endpoint:model` so paid siblings stay eligible.
- [ ] AC2 — `proxy/docs/routing.md` states the consequences: the quarantine
      is persisted in `provider-state.json`, feeds the exhaustion
      `retry_after`, and is consulted by chain-hold (hold when it fits the
      budget, immediate accurate `retry_after` when it does not).
- [ ] AC3 — The `respect_ratelimit_headers` comment blocks in
      `proxy/config.yaml` (the per-entry documentation block and the
      `server.*` block) mention the account quarantine and the two margins.
- [ ] AC4 — The provider-fallback cooldown list in `proxy/README.md` gains a
      bullet for the reset-aware account quarantine, adjacent to the existing
      "Usage-limit quarantine" bullet.
- [ ] AC5 — Documented behaviour matches the merged implementation exactly:
      every statement is verified against the code, and no undocumented knob
      is invented.

## Minimal implementation

- Extend the existing "Upstream rate-limit headers" section in
  `proxy/docs/routing.md` with an account-scoped subsection (bullet list, no
  new headings beyond one `####`).
- Add two to three comment lines to each of the two `respect_ratelimit_headers`
  blocks in `proxy/config.yaml`.
- Add one bullet to the cooldown list in `proxy/README.md`.

## Constraints

- UK English; match the surrounding prose style and bullet format.
- No new configuration keys; document only what exists.
- Do not restate the LP-0MVBHDNLB007ALLJ parsing rules in full — link by
  reference instead.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/docs/routing.md` — canonical behaviour reference for rate-limit
  headers and cooldowns.
- `proxy/config.yaml` — operator-facing documentation of the provider entry
  and `server.*` flags.
- `proxy/README.md` — provider-fallback cooldown/quarantine summary list.
- `proxy/proxy/provider.py` — read-only verification of documented behaviour.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the implementation item (docs must describe merged behaviour).

## Deliverables

- Updated docs and config comments.
- Commit recorded on this work item.
data.title: Docs: reset-aware account quarantine
